Claire: Heads up — we're seeing situations where streaming reconnects are consuming burst credits twice. Repro steps in prod-ish tenant A.
Ben: Ugh. Is this the partial-token accounting bug we thought was fixed?
Claire: Similar but different. Flow: client opens stream, gets burst-credits reservation, then disconnects mid-response. Client reconnects with resume token and server re-reserves credits as if it's a new stream.
Dan: That sounds like 'reservation not tied to resume_id' — we should be reconciling by resume_id when available.
Ellie: Can we hold a sticky reservation keyed by (org_id, key_id, resume_id) so reconnects reuse the same reservation? Or would that block others? :thinking_face:
Ben: If resume_id is untrusted (client could replay), we need to validate resume token or have short sticky reservation TTL.
Jen: Proposal: reserve credits at start but mark them 'sticky' for 30s keyed to resume_id. If a reconnect with same resume_id happens within TTL, reuse credits and adjust accounting. After TTL, release leftover credits back to org pool.
Riley: Ops concern: race where original connection *also* finishes and releases credits while reconnect reclaims them. We need an atomic compare-and-swap in the ledger.
Dan: True. Implementation idea: ledger entries have state enum {reserved, attached, released}. On reserve we write reserved->(resume_id=null). On attach (first token sent) we set attach with resume_id. Reconnect attempts to CAS from reserved with matching resume_id.
Claire: What about fairness? If someone keeps opening multiple short streams to hog sticky reservations they could starve others.
Ellie: Add per-key sticky_count limit and global sticky budget per org. Default sticky_count=2, sticky_budget=burst_quota * 0.2.
Ben: Also needs telemetry: dashboard metrics for sticky_reservations_active, sticky_reserve_hits/misses, double-charged-events. Can we add a graph per-org in Console?
Jen: I'll add telemetry tags: org_id, key_hash, resume_id_present (bool), reconnect_latency_ms. We can surface top offenders.
Riley: On the revert side, we should also handle partial tokens: if disconnect happened mid-token, how do we bill? We currently bill when tokens are emitted; partial tokens counted via last_ack position. Reconnect should carry last_ack so we don't duplicate token billing.
Dan: Right — client should include last_ack_token_index in resume request. Server will compute outstanding = total_emitted - last_ack and charge only outstanding if reservation hasn't already been applied.
Claire: Edge-case: client reconnects to different region where model variant differs; resumed stream may have different per-token cost. What then?
Ben: We can normalize by using the original route's cost profile attached to the reservation. If the route changed, charge diff on fallback path but allow resume only to compatible variants; otherwise force new stream (no resume) and release reservation.
Ellie: UX: Console should show a 'sticky resume' toggle per org and a rate-limit policy inspector that explains how sticky reservations are accounted in the billing UI.
Jen: For rollout: feature flag behind rollout/sticky-reserve with canary to 5% of orgs + our internal test tenants. We'll also add an alert for "double-charge anomalies > 0.1%".
Riley: I'll add an oncall playbook snippet. infra-bot, create monitor for "streaming_double_charge_rate > 0.001" across prod clusters.
infra-bot: monitor "streaming_double_charge_rate" created in prod with threshold 0.001 and pager duty escalation to "streaming-oncall". :white_check_mark:
Claire: Next steps: Dan and Ben to prototype ledger CAS and TTL eviction. Jen + Ellie handle telemetry + Console surfaces. Riley will wire alert and runbook. I'll coordinate canary.
Ben: Will sketch a small sequence diagram and a pseudo-API for resume validation. Example resume request body:

```
POST /v1/streams/resume
{
  "resume_id": "r_abc123",
  "key_id": "k_prod_01",
  "last_ack_index": 42
}
```

Claire: Good. Keep messages short in PRs and include perf test for reconnect storm (1000 reconnects/min) so we can measure fairness.
Dan: I'll push a design doc later today.
Ellie: Thanks team. :rocket:
Ben: cc @security for resume token validation review.
Jen: tagging @billing for accounting sign-off on release plan.
Claire: End.
